subject: Mental Models
title: Sensitive Dependence
description: A quick, practical guide to Sensitive Dependence.

hook.text: Edward Lorenz ran a weather model twice. He rounded one number by 0.0001.

buildup.text: Sensitive dependence on initial conditions means tiny input differences produce vastly different outcomes over time.

discovery.text: This is the butterfly effect: a butterfly flapping its wings in Brazil could theoretically trigger a tornado in Texas.

twist.text: Sensitive dependence makes long-term prediction impossible in some systems. No amount of data fixes it—.

punchline.text: Tiny differences compound into chaos. Prepare instead of predicting.

quiz.question: What does sensitive dependence on initial conditions imply for prediction?
options: Long-term prediction becomes impossible because tiny differences amplify wildly
